about: Bad patterns the critics hunt for. 'detect' lists the automated signals (computed by studio/server/qa) that raise the finding; 'fix' lists preferred remedies in priority order.

patterns.name: Feature bloat
patterns.definition: A system exists because it sounded realistic but creates no meaningful decision.
detect: feature score < 3.0 on the anti-bloat rubric
action used in < 2% of bot turns across all strategies
system's variables never change any outcome metric by > 1% in sensitivity runs
fix: abstract into a single driver of another metric

patterns.name: Dashboard syndrome
patterns.definition: The game feels like corporate analytics software instead of a game.
detect: home screen shows > 5 headline numbers
home screen first viewport is > 50% tables
no primary action visible above the fold
no imagery/visualization on primary screens
fix: home = needs-you queue + next moment + ≤4 numbers + primary actions
replace tables with cards/maps/boards where entities have identity

patterns.name: Number soup
patterns.definition: Many statistics move, but the player does not understand why.
detect: metric shown on a primary screen without declared drivers
> 12 distinct numbers in first viewport
metric changes > 20% in a tick with no news/explanation emitted
fix: declare drivers for every headline metric and render Why?
aggregate into one index with drilldown
emit a consequence card after big changes

patterns.name: False depth
patterns.definition: There are many screens, but few interesting strategic choices.
detect: screens / distinct player actions ratio > 1.5
screens with zero actions and no unique information
fix: attach actions to the information that motivates them

patterns.name: Redundant systems
patterns.definition: Two or more mechanics effectively represent the same decision.
detect: two actions with > 0.9 correlated effects on all outcome metrics in sensitivity runs
two screens listing the same entity set with the same columns
fix: merge into one action with a parameter
make them trade off along different axes

patterns.name: Click burden
patterns.definition: Routine tasks require excessive navigation or repeated manual input.
detect: bot needs > 6 actions per tick on average to keep the business healthy
same action repeated on > 5 entities per tick by the conservative bot

patterns.name: Weak consequence visibility
patterns.definition: Player actions affect hidden variables without understandable feedback.
detect: action has no preview
action effects only touch fields not shown on any screen
no consequence card/news after action

patterns.name: Menu maze
patterns.definition: Important actions are buried behind navigation.
detect: > 7 top-level destinations
primary loop action requires > 2 clicks from home
needs-you items not linked to the action that resolves them
fix: actions on home and in inspectors

patterns.name: Micromanagement without payoff
patterns.definition: The player manages details that do not meaningfully affect outcomes.
detect: parameter sensitivity: varying a player-controlled field ±50% changes profit < 2%
fix: raise its impact so it becomes a real tradeoff

patterns.name: Notification fatigue
patterns.definition: Too many alerts cause important events to disappear into noise.
detect: > 3 interrupting (critical) events per in-game month
> 25 inbox items per in-game month
critical share of events > 15%
fix: priority tiers: critical / important / routine / background

patterns.name: Passive simulation
patterns.definition: The world changes, but the player rarely makes meaningful choices.
detect: minimal-intervention bot achieves ≥ 85% of the active bots' median score
> 8 consecutive ticks with no needs-you items or available new opportunity

patterns.name: Dominant strategy
patterns.definition: One approach becomes obviously superior.
detect: one bot strategy wins > 70% of seeded runs
one action's usage share > 50% in the best bot
best strategy's median score > 2x second best

patterns.name: Snowballing
patterns.definition: Once ahead, the game becomes impossible to lose.
detect: after year 5, the leading bot's lead keeps growing in > 90% of runs
late-game bankruptcy rate = 0 with near-zero variance
cash growth late game > 3x early game with no new decisions
fix: scale costs (complexity, overhead, regulation scrutiny with market share)

patterns.name: Death spiral
patterns.definition: Once behind, recovery becomes practically impossible.
detect: runs that fall below 30% of starting cash recover in < 10% of cases
bankruptcy follows within 12 ticks of first negative quarter in > 80% of cases
fix: rescue options (restructure, sell assets, emergency investor)

patterns.name: Too many sliders
patterns.definition: The simulation exposes internal variables that should be meaningful decisions.
detect: > 5 numeric inputs on one screen
numeric inputs without a stated tradeoff
fix: replace sliders with 2–4 named options that carry tradeoffs

patterns.name: Fake choice
patterns.definition: Options look different but result in essentially the same consequence.
detect: event choices whose effect vectors differ by < 10%
action options producing identical outcome distributions
fix: differentiate along different resources (cash vs reputation vs time vs relationships)
remove the choice and narrate the outcome

patterns.name: Text walls
patterns.definition: Major gameplay occurs through reading long blocks instead of interacting.
detect: event/onboarding text > 60 words
screen text > 1500 characters in first viewport

patterns.name: Generic visual design
patterns.definition: Every game looks like the same enterprise dashboard with a new title.
detect: theme motif = none
no signature visualization
palette distance to the reference 'dark panel + gold' < threshold
screenshot test: genre not inferable from nav + visuals

patterns.name: Theme–mechanic disconnect
patterns.definition: The game says 'airline' or 'restaurant' but interactions could belong to any business.
detect: < 50% of actions reference genre-specific entity kinds
no genre-specific causal driver in the main economic loop
fix: derive actions from the fantasy verbs
domain-specific drivers (load factor, covers, recoupment, depth chart)

patterns.name: Empty commissioner mode
patterns.definition: Sandbox controls alter superficial values rather than the actual simulation.
detect: commissioner offers toggles only
commissioner edit not reflected in the next tick's computation (test)
fix: schema-driven editors for entities, orgs, markets, rules

patterns.name: Shallow rivals
patterns.definition: Competitors are random-number generators rather than strategic actors.
detect: rival orgs take no actions from the shared action set
rival performance variance unexplained by their strategy
no rival ever reacts to the player
fix: archetype strategies using the same action set
lifecycle: grow, decline, merge, fail, change leadership

patterns.name: Static world
patterns.definition: The economy and industry do not evolve meaningfully.
detect: world variables with zero variance over 10 years
no new orgs/entities entering after start
segment preferences constant

patterns.name: Unclear core loop
patterns.definition: A new player does not understand what is fun or what to do.
detect: no onboarding steps
first primary action not highlighted
first 5 minutes: bot following onboarding can't complete the first loop

patterns.name: Setup front-loading
patterns.definition: Long configuration wizards ask questions a new player cannot yet answer.
detect: new-game setup > 2 steps or > 6 inputs before play

patterns.name: Online dependency
patterns.definition: A portable game silently depends on the network.
detect: external <link>/<script>/fetch URLs in release build
